skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False severity=minor: Checked AR2025 p.110 and AR2024 p.130 (note 5.2). Same line item in both years: 'Purchase obligations relating to contract manufacturers', inside 'Contractual obligations not recognised in the balance sheet', undiscounted and not risk-adjusted, so off-balance-sheet in every year compared and not capitalized. Figures are right: DKK 33,107m (2023), 71,061m (2024, same figure in both reports), 91,031m (2025). 91,031/33,107 = 2.75x; 91,031/309,064 = 29.5% (AR2025 p.83). The Q2 2026 DKK ~3bn 'right-sizing of manufacturing capacity agreements' is on 6-K p.13 and sits inside adjusted gross margin (78.2%). Per-share math holds: 3,000 x 0.78 / 4,448 = DKK 0.53 (0.53 also on the Q2 2026 diluted count of 4,435.8m, 6-K p.38). Three framing problems. (1) The 2023 to 2025 comparison skips 2024. Most of the increase came in 2024 (+DKK 37,954m, +115%) while sales grew 25.0%. 2025 added only +DKK 19,970m (+28%) on +6.4% sales. So the stock was mostly signed in the growth year, not 'just as sales growth turned negative'. Negative growth is the 2026 guide (AR2025 p.16); 2025 reported growth was +6.4%. (2) '29% of a year's sales' sets a multi-year undiscounted stock against one year's flow. The current portion is DKK 15,746m, 5.1% of 2025 sales, and the other DKK 75,285m falls due after more than one year. (3) The 'further DKK 3-9bn' rests on an assumed 10% surplus share that nothing on these pages supports. The 6-K does not say which agreements the DKK 3bn relates to, so tying it to this line item is an inference. Correction: CMO purchase obligations (off-balance-sheet, undiscounted) rose DKK 33.1bn -> 71.1bn -> 91.0bn over 2023-2025. Most of the rise was in 2024 (+115% on +25% sales); 2025 was +28% on +6.4% sales. DKK 15.7bn falls due within a year, 5.1% of 2025 sales. A DKK ~3bn capacity-agreement right-sizing cost hit Q2 2026 adjusted gross margin (2.3% of 2025 EBIT, ~DKK 0.53/share after tax). Any further charge is unquantified.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=False severity=minor: Re-read AR2025 p.110 and the other skeptic's pages. The 6-K Q2 2026 p.14 H1 text repeats 'one-time costs related to right-sizing of manufacturing capacity agreements'. CMD manufacturing p.10 defines CMO in an oral-capacity roadmap. Sizing the narrowed claim, all in DKK and undiscounted: total stock 91,031m = 29.5% of 2025 net sales (309,064) and 71.3% of 2025 operating profit (127,658, AR2025 p.83). The portion due within a year is 15,746m = 5.1% of sales and 12.3% of EBIT. These are payment obligations, not losses. Only the surplus share becomes a charge, and nothing discloses it. Sensitivity: each 10% of the total stock found surplus is about DKK 9.1bn (7.1% of 2025 EBIT, about DKK 1.60/share after 22% tax on 4,435.8m diluted shares, 6-K p.38). Each 10% of the current portion is DKK 1.6bn (1.2% of EBIT). The one realised data point is the Q2 2026 charge of about DKK 3bn: 3.3% of the stock, 2.3% of 2025 EBIT, about DKK 0.53/share after tax. Correction: Contract-manufacturer purchase obligations of DKK 91.0bn (off-balance-sheet, undiscounted, 71% of 2025 EBIT; DKK 15.7bn due within 12 months) were mostly committed in 2024. Settling the first part cost about DKK 3bn in Q2 2026. Every further 10% of the stock found surplus would cost about DKK 9bn, about 7% of EBIT. The surplus share is undisclosed. Conceded: The right-sizing charge itself is disclosed: 6-K p.13 and p.14, and CFO prepared remarks on the grade-C 2026Q2 call. Only the stock is undiscussed. Agreed. Held: The 2023-to-2025 framing stays corrected: most of the build was in 2024 at +25% sales growth. The 29.5%-of-sales ratio sets a multi-year stock against one year of sales. Narrowed: Sized as asked. Due-within-a-year DKK 15.7bn = 5.1% of sales and 12.3% of EBIT as a cash obligation. The loss exposure is about DKK 9.1bn per 10% of the stock found surplus. Material in scale; the probability is unknown.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=False severity=minor: The DKK 3bn 'right-sizing of manufacturing capacity agreements' charge is not hidden: it is in the Q2 2026 6-K MD&A (NVO:6k/2026-08-04_caq22026.md p13, and again in H1 text p14) and was read out in the CFO's prepared remarks on the 2026Q2 call (NVO:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p1, grade C, Karsten Munk Knudsen). So the existence of a CMO exit cost is management-voiced. What no source in the index addresses is the stock: the DKK 91.0bn purchase obligation to contract manufacturers (AR2025 p110) vs DKK 33.1bn (AR2024 p130). The only analyst supply question on the 2026Q2 call (Richard Vosser, JPM) asked about API plant utilisation, not CMO commitments; the 2025Q4 call question was about supply shortfall risk for the Wegovy pill (opposite direction). Searched 'contract manufactur', 'capacity agreement', 'right-siz', 'CMO', 'onerous', 'overcapacity' across all NVO transcripts including the Bloomberg-licensed 2026Q1 call (label: Novo Nordisk 2026Q1 earnings call (Bloomberg)): no hit beyond the prepared-remark line and a 2024Q4 Catalent remark about 'pre-existing CMO contracts'. skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=False severity=major: Rechecked against the other skeptic's 2023-2024-2025 path. AR2024 p130 carries the DKK 33,107m comparative, AR2025 p110 the 2025 figure of DKK 91,031m (current 15,746m), and the other skeptic's 2024 figure of 71,061m fits that series, so most of the build was signed in 2024, during the supply shortage. I searched the 2024Q3, 2024Q4, 2025Q1 and 2025Q2 calls for whether that build was discussed. It was, but only as strategy. In 2024Q3 prepared remarks Novo is 'investing in internal and external capacity to increase supply both short and long term' (NVO:companies/NVO/transcripts/2024Q3_transcript.md p8). In 2024Q3 Q&A Mattias Häggblom (Handelsbanken) asked about external CDMO sourcing for cagrilintide and the plan B if Catalent were blocked, and the CFO answered 'continue to contract external capacity' (p18). In 2024Q4 Camilla Sylvest said Catalent would add supply 'beyond our pre-existing CMO contracts' (NVO:companies/NVO/transcripts/2024Q4_transcript.md p2). Correction: Novo's 2024 strategy of contracting external fill-finish capacity was openly stated on the 2024Q3-2024Q4 calls. The non-obvious part is only this: the off-balance-sheet stock that strategy left behind (DKK 71bn at end-2024, DKK 91bn at end-2025, of which DKK 15.7bn falls due within a year) has never been sized on a call or set against the DKK ~3bn right-sizing charge of 2026, and consensus at the guidance midpoint shows no further exit cost priced. The 2024 contracting was not hidden: management said on the 2024Q3 and 2024Q4 calls that it was contracting external capacity. My round 1 phrase 'no source discusses' was too broad for the build itself. I am raising my severity from minor to major. Held: Held as not refuted. Discussion of the build was always about adding supply (shortage era). No call, release or CMD page gives the DKK 71-91bn stock or asks about a surplus, even after the 2026 right-sizing charge. That gap between a stated strategy and an unsized liability is still the least obvious item on NVO. Narrowed: Narrowed from 'commitments never discussed' to 'the size of the commitment stock and its overhang relative to the first right-sizing charge was never discussed'. skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False severity=major: Numbers are on the pages. Receivables are DKK 88,949m at 30 Jun 2026 (6-K Q2 2026 p.29) and 69,575m at 30 Jun 2025 (6-K Q2 2025 p.31), +27.8%. Q2 net sales are 78,488 (p.4) vs 76,857 (Q2 2025 p.15), +2.1% reported. Year on year is the right seasonal basis, but the DSO math has three problems. (1) Basis. AR2025 p.89 says 'Wholesaler charge-backs remain netted against trade receivable balances'. Managed Care, Medicare and Medicaid rebates sit in a separate liability, and US deductions are 70% of US gross sales (p.88). So receivables are close to gross invoice value, while the denominator is net sales. Any widening of gross-to-net raises 'DSO' with no change in collection. Q2 2026 US Wegovy injectable prices fell 22% (p.10). The sales-deduction liability went from DKK 134,400m at Dec 2025 to 141,730m at Jun 2026 (p.29, current + non-current) even after the DKK 26,760m 340B release, an underlying build of ~DKK 34bn that exceeds the DKK 18bn receivables build. That fits gross invoicing outpacing net sales. It is not proof of channel stuffing. (2) Timing. Sequentially, the step is in Q1 2026, not Q2. On the same x91 basis: Dec 2024 71,949/85,683 = 76 days; Jun 2025 82; Dec 2025 70,856/79,144 = 81; Mar 2026 82,565/70,063 adjusted (6-K Q1 p.27, p.12) = 107; Jun 2026 103. DSO fell in Q2, the quarter whose pipeline fill the candidate cites. (3) Magnitude. The cited pipeline fill is Wegovy pill outside the US, DKK 77m (p.10). The US Ozempic pill/Rybelsus line was DKK 2,273m, +7% CER, i.e. ~DKK 0.15bn incremental (p.31). Together that is <2% of the DKK 17.9bn 'excess'. Cash flow cuts against a quality problem in Q2: Q2 operating cash flow was DKK 55,199m vs 41,774m (p.38), and working capital released ~DKK 13.3bn in Q2 (H1 -19,912 vs Q1 -33,231; p.28 and Q1 p.26). Inventory: DKK 51,352m prints at both 31 Mar and 30 Jun 2026. Both balance sheets foot to their totals with that figure (Q1 current assets 177,317; Q2 208,696), so it is in the indexed filing text and is not an index extraction slip. Whether the filing itself is wrong cannot be checked from these sources. Factoring (US 3,812 + Japan 1,747 = DKK 5,559m) is a Dec 2025 figure (AR2025 p.102), not June. The Lilly DSO of 79.5 sets a 6-month receivable change against year-on-year revenue and a different gross-to-net profile, so it is not a comparable item. Correction: Trade receivables (gross of most US rebates) rose to DKK 88.9bn at 30 Jun 2026, +28% YoY, against +2% reported Q2 sales. The step-up happened in Q1 2026 (DKK 70.9bn -> 82.6bn), and receivables/net-sales days eased slightly in Q2 (~107 -> ~103). Pipeline fill explains well under DKK 0.5bn of it. A widening gross-to-net ratio is a plausible mechanical cause, and Q2 operating cash flow (DKK 55.2bn) does not show a collection problem. Treat this as a monitoring item, not a DKK 18bn excess.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=True severity=major: I tested whether any version survives once the basis is fixed. (1) Gross basis. AR2025 p.89: only charge-backs are netted in receivables, and rebates sit in 'Sales deductions and product returns'. On a like-for-like basis, Dec 2025 vs Jun 2026 (6-K p.29), receivables rose DKK 18,093m (70,856 -> 88,949). The deduction liability ex-340B rose DKK 34,090m: 134,400 - 26,760 = 107,640 -> 141,730 (140,201 current + 1,529 non-current). The net trade position (receivables minus rebate liability) went from DKK -36,784m to -52,781m. Novo owes customers DKK 16bn more, net, than six months earlier. There is no DSO 'excess' on a net basis. (2) The other skeptic's p.15 cite is correct and changes my round-1 cash-flow point. H1 FCF rose to DKK 55.3bn 'driven by phasing of operating expenses, timing of US rebate payments and tax payments'. Tax payables also rose DKK 12,044m (8,416 -> 20,460, p.29). So the Q2 working-capital release and the strong Q2 operating cash flow (DKK 55,199m, p.38) are payment timing, not evidence of clean collections. (3) Seasonality check. H1 2025 on the old presentation: provisions fell DKK 8,202m (120,329 -> 112,127), of which ~3bn was the 340B cut. Trade payables, which then held confirmed rebates, were flat (28,846 -> 28,206) (6-K Q2 2025 p.31). So H1 2025 saw a ~DKK 5bn fall and H1 2026 a ~DKK 34bn rise ex-340B. This is not seasonal. (4) Pipeline fill. The grade-C 2026Q1 call (p.15, CFO) says 'to the tune of $150 million' of Q1 Wegovy pill sales. In USD that is about DKK 1bn; if it was mis-transcribed from DKK, DKK 150m. Either way it is ≤6% of the DKK 18bn. Conclusion: the receivables/DSO version is not material as a revenue-quality or collection signal once rebates are netted. The material version is a different claim: H1 2026 FCF is flattered by deferred US rebate payments. Correction: Withdraw receivables-vs-sales DSO as the signal. Replace with: the US rebate liability excluding the 340B release grew about DKK 34bn in H1 2026 (vs about a DKK 5bn decline in H1 2025), and the 6-K credits rebate payment timing for part of the H1 FCF rise to DKK 55.3bn. Some of that FCF should reverse when the rebates are paid. The size of that reversal is undisclosed, but the swing is about 11% of 2025 sales. Conceded: Pipeline fill was asked and answered (2026Q1 call p.15, grade C: about $150m, 'absolutely normal'). The 6-K p.15 attributes H1 FCF partly to 'timing of US rebate payments'. That second point overturns my round-1 use of Q2 operating cash flow as proof of healthy collections. Held: The DSO of ~82 to ~103 days divides near-gross receivables by net sales and is not a valid basis. The step-up is in Q1 2026, not Q2. No version where receivables alone signal DKK 18bn of borrowed sales survives the netting. Narrowed: I disagree with the other skeptic's narrowed c02 (receivables build/DSO as the non-obvious point). It fails on materiality after netting, so refuted=true for the candidate as written and as they narrowed it. A replacement candidate (FCF flattered by a ~DKK 34bn ex-340B rebate-liability build) would need its own read.

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False severity=major: Verified: Proclamation 11020 p.1 ('zero until January 20, 2029' applies to companies with MFN agreements and approved onshoring plans; '15 percent for products of ... the European Union, unless a lower rate applies'). AR2025 p.89: DKK 318,586m PP&E + intangibles ex goodwill, Denmark 194,790 (61.1%), US 77,394 (24.3%); US sales 173,166 (56.0%). The WH fact sheet gives USD 10bn vs USD 27bn+. The duty arithmetic is right (0.15 x 0.5 x 0.30 x 173,166 = DKK 3,896m = 3.1% of 2025 EBIT), but both drivers are undisclosed assumptions: the 50% import share and a customs value of 30% of net sales. Customs value is a transfer price, and if semaglutide enters as API or bulk for US fill-finish (Novo bought three Catalent fill-finish sites, AR2025 p.110, and US assets rose from DKK 49,305m to 77,394m in 2025, p.89), it could be far below 30% of net sales. The base is 2025 US sales applied to 2029 after a guided 2026 decline. The 15% only applies if the post-2029 MFN zero rate is not extended. The 'DKK 2-6bn' range is therefore an assumption range, not a measurement. Separately, the IRA comparison (79.9% vs 15.3%) uses each brand's global sales (AR2025 p.90), but IRA prices apply only to US Medicare. As written it measures brand concentration, not IRA exposure. It is like-for-like across the two companies but overstates both. Correction: Novo's PP&E/intangible base is 61% Denmark vs 56% US sales, and its US manufacturing pledge (USD 10bn) is below Lilly's (USD 27bn+). A post-January 2029 EU-origin duty of up to 15% is a real but unquantifiable risk: import share and customs value are not disclosed, and the US asset base grew 57% in 2025.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=False severity=major: Sizing the footprint version (AR2025 p.89, DKK): Denmark held 194,790 of 318,586 (61.1%) in 2025 vs 164,744 of 252,484 (65.2%) in 2024. US 77,394 (24.3%) vs 49,305 (19.5%). US assets grew DKK 28.1bn (+57%) in one year, so the 'Denmark-heavy' gap is closing fast, before the 2029 date. A footprint share is a level, not a cost. It turns into money only through import share and customs value, and neither is disclosed. The USD 10bn vs USD 27bn+ pledges (WH fact sheet p.1) are like-for-like announced amounts, though neither is broken out in the filings. Correction: Novo's non-goodwill long-lived assets are 61% Danish (down from 65%) against 56% US sales. US assets grew 57% in 2025. The post-January 2029 duty exposure is real but unsizeable from disclosed data. Conceded: The exemption and its end date are public headlines, and the issue is common to EU-made names. Held: The DKK 2-6bn duty range is an assumption range, and the IRA 80% vs 15% uses global brand sales. Narrowed: Footprint version: unsized. The trend (65% -> 61% Denmark) cuts against the cliff framing.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=False severity=major: The tariff exemption itself is a press-release headline: 'Novo Nordisk is expected to receive a three-year tariff exemption' (NVO:policy/press_2025-11-06_us_administration_agreement.md p1), tariffs are a named risk in AR2025 p41 and the outlook assumptions (AR2025 p17; NVO:6k/2026-08-04_caq22026.md p17), and the CFO addressed tariffs in 2025Q1 prepared remarks ('a potential expansion or increase of tariffs may have a negative impact', NVO:companies/NVO/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p9, grade C). Section 232 pharma tariffs and the 2029 grace expiry apply to every EU-manufacturing name on the shortlist, which makes the generic point obvious. Searched 'tariff', 'Section 232', 'grace period', '2029' in 2025Q3, 2025Q4, 2026Q1 (+Bloomberg), 2026Q2 transcripts: zero hits since 2025Q1, so the post-exemption cliff has not been discussed. The Novo-specific part (61% of PP&E and intangibles in Denmark vs 56% US sales, AR2025 p89; IRA-selected share 80% vs Lilly 15%) is a computed contrast no call or release makes. Correction: Keep only the relative-footprint angle (Denmark asset concentration and modest US investment pledge vs Lilly against an identical 2029 grace expiry); the existence of the exemption and its end date are public headlines, and the duty sizing rests on an undisclosed import-value assumption.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=False severity=major: Round 1 stands. The exemption is a press-release headline and tariffs are a sector-wide theme, but the Denmark-heavy footprint against an identical 2029 expiry is not discussed after 2025Q1. The other skeptic shows the US asset base grew from DKK 49,305m to 77,394m in 2025 (AR2025 p89) and that fill-finish was bought in the US via Catalent (p110). That suggests Novo is already partly onshoring, and management has spoken about its US sites in prepared remarks (2025Q1 call p2: Bloomington and Clayton). Correction: Keep only the relative-footprint contrast (61% of PP&E and intangibles in Denmark vs 56% of sales in the US, and a USD 10bn vs 27bn+ US pledge). Drop the IRA 80% vs 15% contrast, which measures global brand concentration rather than Medicare exposure. Conceded: Conceded that the duty size is an assumption stack, that US assets grew 57% in 2025, and that the IRA comparison uses global brand sales. Held: Held: a 2029 tariff cliff tied to footprint has not been raised on any call since the exemption, and consensus sits at 2026 guidance, which does not reach 2029. Narrowed: Narrowed to the footprint contrast only.

verdict_reason: Novo's property, plant and equipment and intangibles excluding goodwill are 61.1% in Denmark (DKK 194.8bn of 318.6bn at end-2025, down from 65.2% a year earlier) against 56% of sales in the US, and its US manufacturing pledge (USD 10bn) is below Lilly's (USD 27bn+), ahead of the same January 2029 end of the Section 232 zero-tariff window; the duty cost cannot be sized from disclosed data, and US assets grew 57% in 2025 (DKK 49.3bn -> 77.4bn), so the gap is closing. | Both skeptics left c10 not refuted but narrowed, and split on what the narrowed version is worth. Obviousness holds the footprint contrast because no call since 2025Q1 mentions tariffs or the 2029 date, while the exemption itself is a press-release headline. Materiality says the footprint is a level, not a cost, and the trend cuts against a cliff. I opened NVO:reports/annual_report_2025.md p.89: Denmark DKK 194,790m of 318,586m (61.1%) vs 164,744m of 252,484m (65.2%) in 2024; US 77,394m vs 49,305m (+57.0%; 2024 restated for the Catalent purchase price allocation). Both readings are right. The footprint contrast is unrefuted and non-obvious in its Novo-specific form, so it survives narrowed, but it carries no measured impact: the DKK 2-6bn duty range rests on an undisclosed import share and customs value (Proclamation 11020 p.1 sets 15% for EU goods only if the MFN zero rate is not extended), and the IRA 80% vs 15% contrast is dropped because it uses global brand sales. Low materiality: not counted as a material survivor.
